author: VargK
quote:
Apparently, metacritic thought it was appropriate to remove my review despite it being completely legitimate. So here it is again, but a bit truncated.

The soul has been completely stripped out of GTA. The writing is absolutely horrendous. Lucia is the worst character in the franchise, which is actually impressive. Every second you're forced to spend with her, which is most of the game, is insufferable. Jason is a complete doormat who only exists to make his ugly, fat, Latina, girlboss babymama happy and has literally no other qualities.

This isn't GTA. This is "force the male audience to submit to female superiority". It's embarrassingly bad and is the furthest thing from fun that I can imagine.

Avoid.

author: VargK
quote:
Fantasy Life is my all-time favorite 3DS game. I didn't think we would ever get a sequel (not counting the JP-only mobile game), so I was very excited when I saw this get announced. Thankfully, I can say that I was not disappointed.

While I still prefer the original (if only for how fondly I remember it), this game maintains all of its charm while adding some very nice QoL features and brand new game modes.

My only real complaint is the same one I had about the original: Let me date Yuelia. Then it would be a 10/10. But since I know L5 will never add that, it sits at a comfortable 9 for me.
game_title: Fantasy Life i: The Girl Who Steals Time

author: VargK
quote:
I'm a huge fan of Playdead's games (Limbo, Inside), and this looked like that with a bit more color. And that's largely what it is. I'd describe it as a hybrid of Inside and A Boy and His Blob.

Where it falters is in its difficulty, or lack thereof. I wouldn't call it a breeze, but there are no real brain-buster puzzles, and the lack of enemy variety keeps things rather predictable. There are fun ideas at play, and you do unlock new mechanics as you progress, but it's all pretty straightforward.

Where I think it excels the most is in the simplicity of its storytelling. The game uses a fictional language and has almost no dialogue anyway, so the story is told thematically through the environments and the music. The first is what I would expect from a game emulating Playdead's design philosophy, but the second was a very nice addition. There are some very cool moments, thanks in large part to the music.

Overall, it's a very solid game and really deserves more attention than it's received. For anyone who enjoys 2D puzzle platformers, this is a must-have.

author: VargK
quote:
Ironically, Harvestella's biggest weak points are the farming and the dungeon crawling, which are the entire reasons to play a game like this. That's not to say that they're bad, but simply that they're very simplistic. Compared to something like Rune Factory 4, this feels like a prototype.

With that said, I love everything else about the game. All of the side quests are fantastic. The writing is great. The story is engaging and interesting. Most of the characters are really well done. The visuals are very nice, and I Iove the art style and character designs. The soundtrack is genuinely my favorite soundtrack of all time, and that's not something I say lightly.

It's an absolute shame that Square-Enix shot the game in the foot by pricing it at $60. This is NOT a AAA game, and it's absolutely absurd that SE thought they could price it like one. Even though I genuinely love the game, I would recommend only buying it on sale for half off, which is what it should have been sold for in the first place.

I would love to see a more polished take on this genre from the studio (I'm not sure if the story leaves room for a sequel, but a spiritual successor would be nice), but, sadly, I don't think that will happen. Still, for what it is, I do recommend it.

author: VargK
quote: I'm very glad that Nihon Falcom made another stage-based action/platformer. I really wanted to like Gurumin, but it was so janky that I just ended up getting frustrated with it. I can happily say that that's not the case here. While certainly not a perfect game, it is extraordinarily fun, and I really wish there was a sequel/spiritual successor.
